[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Type: Time (Minutes)
- Amount: 45
- Description: Governor craft direction + publication — Agroverse chocolate-process reel v1→v5 (grade, beat order, machine-shots)
  
  Pull requests (GitHub evidence):
  - https://www.instagram.com/reel/DgNAp8ihMM8/
  
  Details:
  GOVERNOR REVIEW, CRAFT DIRECTION AND PUBLICATION — Agroverse chocolate-process reel (v1 -> v5), 2026-11-26.
  
  NOTE ON THE NUMBER: 45 minutes is an ESTIMATE, not a measurement. I can see your messages but not your watching/thinking time. Breakdown of the basis, so you can correct it:
  - 3 full video reviews with frame-specific craft feedback (v1 beat spec, v2/v4 grade + blemish notes, v5 sign-off)
  - 6 substantive direction messages
  - Instagram publication incl. caption authoring
  If the real figure differs, say so and I will file a correcting entry.
  
  WHAT YOUR TIME PRODUCED — this was the discriminating half of the loop, not a rubber stamp. Every one of the following was a correction no automated gate could have made:
  
  1. Rebuilt the beat order from scratch. You rejected the shape of v1: cacao pods GROWING ON TREE must open the film, not a hand breaking a pod. That single note invalidated the entire first cut.
  
  2. Caught a category error the vision model passed. "POD split open is not cacao pod." An open pod was in frame and every structural gate was happy; only domain knowledge knew it was the wrong subject.
  
  3. Fixed a sequence error. Crack-open-by-hand had to FOLLOW clip-from-tree — an ordering judgement about causality in the process, invisible to per-clip labelling.
  
  4. Specified the winnowing beat precisely: must show the MACHINE — beans poured in, nibs come out. This converted the weakest beat (1/3 confidence) into a 3/3 verified pair, and is now an SOP rule.
  
  5. Resolved the gate #6 collision with Option B — extend the beat with an establishing shot rather than reorder the spec. A judgement call between two legitimate constraints; not something to be decided unilaterally by the agent.
  
  6. Caught a GRADE failure that no assertion in the tool can detect. "The cacao in frame is bulk low grade cacao... clear brown instead of the dark black dirty look." Verified independently by vision grading: the v4 drying clip read "dark greyish-black, mottled with white mould and dirt." Bulk lot in a premium brand film — a commercial trust error, and it was invisible to all 8 structural gates plus action-level QC.
  
  7. Caught a blemish in the hero shot. "Replace with cacao pods that don't have blemish on their surface" — first-frame presentation quality on the feed thumbnail.
  
  WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE REEL:
  This thread's failure pattern is now the basis for new tooling — the window-sample QC gate and a grade/condition check. The general finding: structural gates (caption length, brand, language, frame-0 human) all passed on a film whose BEATS WERE WRONG 12 out of 12 times. Correctness of depiction and quality of subject are not captured by any existing assertion. Your review caught both classes before an audience did.
  
  Outcome shipped: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DgNAp8ihMM8/
  
- Contributor(s): Gary Teh
- TDG Issued: 75.00
- Attached Filename: N/A
- Destination Contribution File Location: N/A
